title: Urgent reroute and soft-warmup controller for token drought
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several high-value customers reported abrupt first-token lag and sustained tokens/sec regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Symptoms include elevated TTFT for short prompts, token emission stalls at ~20-40% of baseline on affected variants, and partial region-dependent recovery when we manually rerouted traffic. The issue appears correlated with simultaneous variant probing and an aggressive cold-start path that bypasses the soft-warmup policy. This ticket implements a short-term safety reroute, a soft-warmup controller to reduce cold-path concurrency, and a protective backlog limiter to restore tokens/sec and TTFT SLOs while we root-cause further.
repro_steps: 1) Use short prompts (<= 32 tokens) against model-variant candidates in prod routing with priority fanout enabled
2) Trigger variant probing ramp (simulate 10x probe weight for new variant) while under 60% core utilization
3) Observe TTFT increase in telemetry (first_byte_latency metric) and tokens/sec drop in per-worker metrics over next 2-4 minutes
4) Reproduce on hosted and private clusters by toggling variant probe weight in router rules
investigation_notes: Telemetry: first_byte_latency and token_emission_rate show coordinated drop across multiple workers; regional dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ttft/ttft-wave (internal)
Heap/flame: worker CPU shows long tail on kernel selection path and KV-cache warmup serialization when probe concurrency > 6
Hypothesis: rushed kernel selection + concurrent cold-weight model probing causes excessive synchronous warmup (weights/kcache) leading to head-of-line stalls for short requests
Observed mitigation: manual reroute to stable variant immediately recovered tokens/sec to ~95% baseline within 40-90s
Customer escalations: 3 priority enterprise tickets (Customer A, B, C) opened with support — all cited degraded interactive experience
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): Apply routing safety rule that routes probe traffic to isolated warmup pool and reduce probe concurrency to 1 for affected models (live rollout 2026-03-10 03:30 UTC)
Deploy soft-warmup controller: lightweight admission controller that serializes weight fetch + small async prefetch; limits in-flight warmup tasks per-worker to 2
Add backlog limiter: drop-to-shed for low-priority probe requests when per-worker emission rate < 50% of baseline
Fallback policy: if tokens/sec does not recover within 3 minutes, auto-failover to next compatible stable variant and notify SRE channel
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy soft-warmup controller to 2 workers in hosted us-west-2 with feature flag soft_warmup.v1=true (1 hour observation)
Stage 2: expand to dedicated clusters with low-traffic pool (3 hours), monitor first_byte_latency and token_emission_rate
